insights.text: Matthew Honnibal's rebuttal of MIT CSAIL's 'Weight-Space Programming' result finds only 3 of 10 experiments actually read raw model weights directly; the flagship Qwen3.5-0.8B fix was done by the model writing Python code to inspect and edit weights, which mech-interp commenters identify as standard directional ablation.

Postman's desktop app silently installs AI agent plugins into Codex and Claude Code, and its own installer writes the trust hash that approves the resulting hook — self-approving the exact consent step meant to stop silent third-party code execution.

Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source system that cryptographically proves which model produced a given output using a zkSNARK, at roughly 70-95x the GPU cost of running the model directly, with no deployment plans.

worktrunk, a git-worktree CLI built specifically for running multiple AI coding agents in parallel, debuted at #3 on GitHub Trending, packaging the hand-rolled tmux-plus-worktree technique solo developers have used since before April as a standalone product.

Vercel Labs' agent-desktop accelerated to +3,791 stars on its fourth day of GitHub Trending, its highest single-day gain yet, while thedotmack/claude-mem posted its lowest tracked daily velocity (+1,139) across a six-day run.

Today's Google Play Store top-30 capture shows zero frontier-lab apps (Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, Grok all absent) for the first time since the appearance/disappearance tracking thread began on October 29.
Simon Willison published a follow-up post running weight interpretation on Qwen 3.8 27B locally, extending the same-week scrutiny of whether models can genuinely read and edit neural network weights.
mattpocock/skills continued its steady GitHub Trending climb to 311,747 stars (+1,164 today), up from 308,701 three days earlier.
